title: Riyadh airport reopens under Houthi threat
credits: Photos: Wolfgang Hasselmann / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Saudi Arabia has partly reopened Riyadh's main airport, despite fresh threats from Yemen's Houthis.
King Khalid International Airport had been closed since the tenth of October.
An attack that day, claimed by the Houthis, reportedly killed thirteen people and injured more than three hundred.
On Sunday, Terminal One reopened for domestic flights, and Terminal Two for international flights by Saudi airlines.
Hours earlier, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree warned airlines and passengers that the airport was a military target, and unsafe.
The Houthis say they fired missiles at the airport, an air base in Khamis Mushait, and a naval base in Jazan.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted twelve missiles and two drones.
Falling debris injured two people in the south of the kingdom, according to civil defence.
The Houthis say their attacks respond to Saudi strikes on Sanaa and other areas, which they say killed or wounded dozens.
The fighting has broken a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since twenty twenty-two.
Hundreds of thousands of Pakistanis live and work in Saudi Arabia, and many fly through Riyadh.
